title: Relative object descent characterizes representable local finite presentation
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $p:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be a morphism of categories fibred in groupoids on $S$-schemes: each has groupoid fibres and cartesian lifts along every base morphism, and $p$ commutes with pullback up to the cartesian isomorphisms. Suppose $p$ is representable by algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], meaning that for each $S$-scheme $B$ and $y\in\mathcal G(B)$ the groupoid of pairs $(x,\gamma:p(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}y|_V)$ over $V\to B$ is represented by an algebraic space $W_y\to B$. Then all $W_y\to B$ are locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] if and only if the following relative object-descent property holds. For every small nonempty directed inverse system of affine $S$-schemes $(T_i)$ with limit $T$, every index $i$, every $y_i\in\mathcal G(T_i)$, every $x\in\mathcal F(T)$ and every isomorphism $\gamma:p(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_T$, there exist $j\ge i$, $x_j\in\mathcal F(T_j)$ and isomorphisms $\alpha:x_j|_T\xrightarrow{\sim}x$, $\beta:p(x_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_{T_j}$ such that $\beta|_T=\gamma\circ p(\alpha)$ under the cartesian pullback identifications. No stack or finiteness assumption on $\mathcal F$ or $\mathcal G$ is required.

source.place: Tag 06CX (lemma-representable-by-spaces-limit-preserving), with limit preservation on objects written out as in section-limit-preserving.

proof.text: Unpack the representing space in the hypothesis. For $y\in\mathcal G(B)$ and $v:V\to B$, points of $W_y(V)$ correspond to isomorphism classes of pairs $(a,\delta)$ with $a\in\mathcal F(V)$ and $\delta:p(a)\xrightarrow{\sim}v^*y$. An arrow from $(a,\delta)$ to $(a',\delta')$ is an isomorphism $u:a\to a'$ with $\delta=\delta'\circ p(u)$. Indeed these are precisely the objects and arrows of the represented groupoid specified in the statement. Its equivalence with the discrete groupoid of points identifies two pairs exactly when such an arrow exists. Restriction of points is pullback of pairs, by naturality of the representation. Thus equality of represented points supplies the compatible isomorphism, rather than merely an isomorphism between their underlying objects. The use of points as evaluations of a sheaf is the convention of [def-trf-algebraic-space].

source.place: Tag 06CX (lemma-representable-by-spaces-limit-preserving), both uses of the 2-Yoneda identification; expanded using the explicit representation hypothesis.

proof.text: Fix a small nonempty directed inverse system of affine $S$-schemes $(T_k)$ with limit $T$, an index $i$, $y_i\in\mathcal G(T_i)$, $x\in\mathcal F(T)$ and an isomorphism $\gamma:p(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_T$. Restrict to the tail $J=\{j:j\ge i\}$. This is small, nonempty and directed, since any common upper bound of two of its indices remains in $J$. It has limit $T$, also over $T_i$. Explicitly a cone on the tail extends to an index $k$ by choosing $j\ge i,k$ and composing its map to $T_j$ with $T_j\to T_k$. A common upper bound proves independence of $j$ and compatibility with transition maps. This extension is inverse to restriction of cones. The same argument with structure maps proves the assertion over $T_i$. No geometric property of transition maps or hypothesis on $S$ is added.

source.place: Tag 06CX, forward implication, restriction to indices j at least i; elementary cone verification.

proof.text: Suppose every representing map is locally of finite presentation. In particular $W_{y_i}\to T_i$ is so. Apply [lem-sfb-space-relative-affine-limit-criterion] with base scheme $T_i$, source $W_{y_i}$, target $T_i$, and the tail system of step 2. All maps to the target over $T_i$ are unique. The displayed bijection therefore gives a class in $\operatorname{colim}_{j\ge i}\operatorname{Mor}_{T_i}(T_j,W_{y_i})$ mapping to the point represented by $(x,\gamma)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise](1) choose a representative $g_j:T_j\to W_{y_i}$. Step 1 represents it by $(x_j,\beta)$ with $\beta:p(x_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_{T_j}$. Equality of its restriction with $(x,\gamma)$ supplies an arrow $\alpha:x_j|_T\xrightarrow{\sim}x$ of pairs. Its defining equation is $\beta|_T=\gamma\circ p(\alpha)$, exactly the requested condition.

source.place: Tag 06CX, forward implication, using spaces-limits.tex Tags 04AK and 06BC to factor the point through a stage.

proof.text: Conversely assume relative object descent. Fix any $S$-scheme $B$ and $y\in\mathcal G(B)$. Take any small nonempty directed affine inverse system $(V_k)$ over $B$ with limit $V$. Forgetting to $S$ retains this limit: for a cone over $S$, the unique scheme factorization respects its structure map by composition with any projection, and that same argument applies to $B$. Given $g:V\to W_y$ over $B$, step 1 represents it by $(x,\delta:p(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}y|_V)$. Choose any index $k$, put $y_k=y|_{V_k}$, and apply the descent hypothesis. It gives $l\ge k$ and $(x_l,\beta)$ with an isomorphism to $(x,\delta)$ after restriction. By step 1 this pair gives $g_l:V_l\to W_y$ whose restriction equals $g$. Hence every map $V\to W_y$ over $B$ descends to a stage. Apply [lem-sfb-space-surjective-affine-limit-criterion] with base $B$, source $W_y$ and target $B$: its target Hom sets are singletons, so the comparison is just the surjective map established above. It follows that $W_y\to B$ is locally of finite presentation. Since $B,y$ were arbitrary, this proves the converse without any descent or finiteness assumption on the two fibred categories.
